advances: Transfers nonnegative Borel mass under actual translations, with an exact affine-span exclusion and one retained baseline. In mixed lattices, the translations preserve the lattice in sum coordinates.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Let $\pi$ project orthogonally onto $V^\perp$ and set $U=\pi(\operatorname{conv}B)$. The cylinder $Z=\pi^{-1}(U)$ is closed. For $\varepsilon>0$ use the source $A_\varepsilon=\{a\in A:\|\pi a\|\ge\varepsilon\}$. Fix $0<\delta<\varepsilon$ and choose a finite $\delta$-net $D\subset B$. The support functions of $U$ and $U_D=\operatorname{conv}(\pi D)$ differ at each $v$ by at most $\delta\|v\|$, because each point of $B$ is within $\delta$ of $D$ and projection contracts distance. List the distinct vertices $p_i$ of $U_D$ and fix one lift $b_i\in D$ for each. For $v=\pi a$, use the smallest maximizing index for $v\cdot p_i$. Its pieces $E_i$ of $A_\varepsilon$ are Borel by finite weak and strict comparisons. On each use $a\mapsto a+b_i$. Its image avoids $Z$ since
$$v\cdot\pi(a+b_i)=\|v\|^2+h_{U_D}(v)\ge h_U(v)+\|v\|(\|v\|-\delta)>h_U(v).$$
For two original points with projections $v,w$ and maximizing indices $i,j$, adding their maximizing inequalities gives $(v-w)\cdot(p_i-p_j)\ge0$. Equal outputs imply $v-w=p_j-p_i$ and hence $p_i=p_j$, so the fixed lift also agrees and the original points agree. This includes ties and a singleton projected polytope. If $V$ is the entire space, all $A_\varepsilon$ are empty and the claim is immediate.

The sets $E_i+b_i$ are disjoint Borel subsets of $(A+B)\setminus Z$. Translation invariance and the pointwise hypothesis give
$$
\int_{(A+B)\setminus Z}F\,d\mathcal H_q
\ge\sum_i\int_{E_i}F(a+b_i)\,d\mathcal H_q(a)
\ge\int_{A_\varepsilon}g\,d\mathcal H_q.
$$
The sets $A_{1/j}$ increase to $A\setminus V$, giving the result by monotone convergence. The translations use actual points of $B$ and therefore preserve sum coordinates in the mixed lattice, including counting measure and intrinsic boundary mass. For $L=a_0+V$, shift $A,P$ by $-a_0$ and the arguments of both functions accordingly, leaving $B$ fixed. In original coordinates the cylinder is $L+\operatorname{conv}B$, which contains $P+B$. Its complement and $P+B$ are disjoint, giving the one-baseline inequality.

statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be nonempty compact sets, $V$ a linear subspace, $q\ge0$ with $\mathcal H_q(A)<\infty$, and $Z=V+\operatorname{conv} B$. Suppose nonnegative Borel functions $F$ on $\mathbb R^m$ and $g$ on $A$ satisfy $F(a+b)\ge g(a)$ for all $a\in A$, $b\in B$. Then
$$
\int_{(A+B)\setminus Z}F\,d\mathcal H_q\ge\int_{A\setminus V}g\,d\mathcal H_q.
$$
For any one compact $P\subseteq A$ contained in an affine subspace $L$ this gives
$$
\int_{A+B}F\,d\mathcal H_q\ge
\int_{P+B}F\,d\mathcal H_q+\int_{A\setminus L}g\,d\mathcal H_q.
$$
The inequalities allow extended integrals and include $q=0$. If $A,B$ lie in $\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, the translated source pieces lie in that lattice as actual sum points.
title: Weighted Hausdorff transfer outside a projected cylinder
